show_hn.title: Show HN: Find overlapping Rust tests with mutation testing
show_hn.story_text:
To tackle the ever-increasing number of tests, I built cargo-test-prune. The idea behind it is to use cargo-mutants to generate mutants, and then solve the set cover problem for those mutants to suggest which tests can be eliminated.
(use a greedy algorithm to cover the detected mutants with fewer tests) I came up with this as a countermeasure against the monotonically increasing tests that tend to accumulate, especially when coding with AI. In fact, this very repository was also written using AI. I ran this tool on a previous revision of this repository. There were 11 tests and 108 generated mutants: 73 were caught by the tests, 23 survived, and 12 failed to compile.
I removed the 5 tests suggested by the tool and re-ran the same 108 mutants. The remaining 6 tests caught the exact same 73

show_hn.title: Show HN: I built Search/Recsys that learns from feedback
show_hn.story_text: Hi HN. A while ago I started building a generic people matching app based on LLM-as-a-judge. I needed a way to bypass the O(n^2) "everyone rates everyone else" trap, but generic RAG was much worse than expected. DNA is a search-like API at the core of that product. It stores one embedding per item (like a vector DB) and gives the best match(es). You evaluate them in some way (LLM / Decision Model / users), and send the score back. This makes it improve in real time, so next time it gives you better results. In my tests, it needed 7x fewer LLM judgments than scoring down the embedding list. Paper in progress. What I don’t know yet is what demo would make you want to try building with it. What would you want to see it do?
